lines.text: First, pricing. Local moves are usually billed by the hour; interstate moves, by weight and distance.
lines.say: First, pricing. Local moves are usually billed by the hour; interstate moves, by weight and distance.

lines.text: Example: 3 movers at $45 an hour each, for 5 hours, is $675.
lines.say: Example: three movers at forty-five dollars an hour each, for five hours, is six hundred seventy-five dollars.

lines.text: Then come extras: stairs, long carries, shuttle trucks and packing.
lines.say: Then come extras: stairs, long carries, shuttle trucks and packing.

lines.text: Interstate estimates are binding, a set price, or non-binding, capping what's due at delivery at 110%.
lines.say: Interstate estimates are binding, a set price, or non-binding, capping what's due at delivery at a hundred and ten percent.

lines.text: Free released value coverage pays 60 cents per pound per item.
lines.say: Free released value coverage pays sixty cents per pound per item.

lines.text: Federal regulators' example: a 10-pound, $1,000 stereo gets 6 bucks. Full value costs extra.
lines.say: Federal regulators' example: a ten-pound, thousand-dollar stereo gets six bucks. Full value costs extra.

post.title: Movers lose a $1,000 stereo. Free coverage pays $6.
post.ig:
Movers lose a $1,000 stereo. The free coverage pays $6.

Local moves are usually billed by the hour (crew x hours); interstate moves are priced by weight and distance, plus extras like stairs, long carries, shuttles and packing.
Under FMCSA rules, a non-binding interstate estimate means the mover can't demand more than 110% at delivery; the rest is billed 30 days later.
Released value coverage is free but pays 60 cents per pound per article: FMCSA's example is a 10-lb, $1,000 stereo paying $6.
Hostage-load complaints rose from 364 in 2017 to 899 in 2020 (FMCSA via AARP).

Sources: FMCSA Protect Your Move, 49 CFR Part 375, This Old House (2025), AARP (2021).
News and education, not financial advice.
